observation: Direct implementation initially bypassed the pipeline agent flow, so review had to recover multiple acceptance and design-contract gaps that should have been caught before build completion.
The builder/reviewer loop resolved the review findings and progress now records review_ready with zero critical, warning, or observation findings.
Review caught a missing synthesized fallback trigger row for no-match behavior, which was necessary for AU5 trigger inspection to explain what happens when no rule matches.
Review caught that Agent behavior was not registered in the Settings sidebar section registry, leaving the new surface present but not fully reachable through existing Settings navigation.
Review caught Settings design-system gaps: the surface needed SplitView persistence plus ItemList/Row selection and Toggle primitives instead of route-local list buttons or raw checkbox controls.
Review caught the missing PATCH mutation rate limit; the route now uses a settings mutation limiter and has an integration test asserting RATE_LIMITED 429 behavior.
Review caught MCP URL editing risk; AU5 now keeps MCP server URL changes read-only and links to Connections as the canonical boundary for service and credential editing.

AU5 validation covered both API behavior and rendered Settings behavior, including fallback rows, built-in rows, validation rejection, secret rejection, route limiting, MCP read-only handoff, and visual proof screenshots.
Changed-file annotation scan found no new TODO, FIXME, or HACK markers in AU5 files; @lore hits were pre-existing context in touched shared Settings and server files.
